boot_evidence: Top-level boot_id is a fresh crypto.randomUUID() created once when worker.js initializes. Do not treat page reload or a stable DevTools target handle as worker restart proof.

result.entries: array of {key,value}, sorted by ECMAScript string comparison

rules: Only the named fields for each operation are accepted. Missing/invalid type gives unsupported_operation; a non-object/array/null or extra field gives invalid_message.
Fresh profile starts at revision 0 with no entries or request history.
Every accepted new put/remove increments revision once, including a same-value put or remove of an absent key. Reads, rejected messages and duplicate requests do not increment revision.
Mutation IDs span put and remove. An exact duplicate type/key/value tuple returns its original successful result without reapplying it; a different tuple under the same ID returns request_conflict.
Both values and request history survive a worker restart. A duplicate response uses the current boot_id with the original operation result.
The first 256 distinct successful mutation IDs are retained. Further new mutations return request_limit. A duplicate of a retained ID still works at the limit.
At most 128 live keys. New-key put at the limit returns entry_limit. Updating/removing an existing key remains valid subject to request_limit.
Keys and values are stored byte-for-byte as JavaScript strings; no trimming, case folding or Unicode normalization. Keys like __proto__ are ordinary data.
A successful mutation is acknowledged only after its state and request receipt have been persisted together. Failure returns storage_failure and does not acknowledge success.
Boot ID changes on actual worker initialization. It is observational metadata excluded only from behavior comparison, never discarded from runtime evidence.

Scope is serial message semantics and persistence after completed acknowledgement. Mid-write forced termination, storage corruption/migration and arbitrary concurrent external writers are not covered.
